item.title: Hold onto that cup o' joe: Study finds moderate caffeine intake may reduce dementia risk
item.description: The study from Mass General Brigham determined that those who drank two to three cups of regular coffee daily, or one to two cups of caffeinated tea, had lower rates of dementia, slower cognitive decline and more preserved cognitive function. Researchers emphasized more work is needed to determine whether a causal link exists between caffeine intake and cognitive function.

item.title: Venezuelan aide to Gov. Healey sues Trump administration to keep her job
item.description: A Venezuelan staffer working for Gov. Maura Healey could lose her job because her H-1B visa is about to expire and the Trump administration has not granted her permanent residency, even though she works full-time and is married to a U.S. citizen, according to court documents.

item.title: State Police Academy staffers face criminal charges in connection with recruit's death
item.description: The state is seeking criminal charges against three full-time instructors and their supervisor at the Massachusetts State Police Academy's Defensive Tactics Unit in connection to the September 2024 death of recruit Enrique Delgado-Garcia.

item.title: Trump administration will not give mistakenly deported Babson student a pathway back to U.S.
item.description: In a court filing on Friday, U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Leah Foley said federal officials "respectfully decline to return Petitioner to the status quo as existed prior to the inadvertent violation" since Any Lucia Lopez Belloza would be subject to removal if she returned to the U.S.

item.title: Man dies, two police officers injured in Fall River shooting
item.description: Nigel Vaughn, 40, was shot and killed by police after officials say he "began to violently resist" during a pat frisk. Two other officers were shot; Both were treated and released from the hospital.

item.title: How 'slow birding' — a new way to bird watch for novices — works
item.description: Bridget Butler, a Vermont birding business owner known as the "Bird Diva," explains how slow birding works and which birds hang around in the wintertime.

item.title: Brainwaves: Why is the brain such a mystery?
item.description: The brain is the organ that makes us who we are. It’s our conduit between reality and thought. But somehow, we’ve only scratched the surface in understanding how the brain actually works.

item.title: World Cup: Which teams play in Boston?
item.description: Three of FIFA's top-ranked teams will play in Gillette during the World Cup. Here's a full schedule of the games coming to Massachusetts.

item.title: World Cup: How to get to Gillette (aka 'Boston') Stadium
item.description: Boston will host games played at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, which is famously not in Boston. You have two main options to make the 30-mile trek: Catch an MBTA Commuter Rail train to Foxboro Station or sit in traffic.
